stories.label: Still Waiting for Peace in Gaza
stories.summary: More than 1,000 Palestinians have been killed since October under a cease-fire that is still called a cease-fire, and Netanyahu has now rejected Trump's 15-point plan for what comes next. Lead with the death toll under the truce, not with the diplomacy: the number is the finding, and it establishes that the agreement regulates the pace of killing rather than ending it. The mechanism our reader should carry is what a cease-fire without an enforcement body actually is — a framework in which one party defines its own violations, so near-daily strikes are reclassified as compliance and the count accumulates with no forum to register it. Then the second layer: Israel's rejection of the 15-point plan means the American proposal had no mechanism to compel acceptance either, which is the same defect one level up. Establish the Gaza health ministry's figure and its period, how many of the dead were children, what specifically in the 15 points Israel rejected (governance, disarmament, withdrawal lines), what Hamas has said, and what the plan proposed for reconstruction and who would administer it. Count Israeli dead in the same period by the same standard. Attribute each casualty figure to the body that issued it. OIC sourcing satisfied: Al Jazeera (QA) carries the rejection framing; the NYT and RT accounts diverge sharply and the divergence is itself reportable.

stories.label: Why Cairo didn't turn up for the Quad defense pact party
stories.summary: Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defense pact in Mecca; Egypt — the Arab world's largest army and the fourth expected signatory — was not on the stage. Lead with the absence, because the story is a realignment told through who is missing: a nuclear-armed South Asian state, the Gulf's financier and the region's most assertive military power have integrated deterrence with each other and not with Cairo. The mechanism our reader should carry is what a defense pact of this kind actually binds — 'joint defense capabilities' and 'strategic deterrence' in the announcement language means force integration, basing access and, in Pakistan's case, an implicit nuclear umbrella, and each of those has a price in sovereignty that a signatory pays quietly. Then Egypt's calculation: Cairo's security financing, its Sinai arrangements and its Gaza mediation role all run through Washington, and joining an axis whose Turkish and Pakistani poles Washington does not control would cost it that position — so the absence may be a veto exercised elsewhere rather than a choice made in Cairo. Establish the pact's actual text and what it commits each party to, what the Saudi deputy public diplomacy minister said on the record, whether Egypt was invited and what Egyptian officials say, the state of Egypt–Turkey and Egypt–Saudi relations, and what this does to the Arab League's dormant joint defense treaty. Who is affected: Pakistan gains a Gulf security patron at the moment its western border is burning, and Egypt is being priced out of a bloc it once assumed it would lead. Mada Masr does its own reporting from Cairo and this is analysis with a named on-the-record anchor — mark interpretation as interpretation. OIC sourcing satisfied: Mada Masr (EG); no Turkish, Saudi or Pakistani outlet carried the pact in this feed, which is a feed-side gap worth auditing given that three OIC states signed it.

stories.label: Rezaei appointed Leader's representative to SNSC
stories.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei has made Mohsen Rezaee — the man who commanded the Revolutionary Guards through the entire Iran–Iraq War — secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and his own representative on it. Lead with the double appointment, because holding both posts is the mechanism: the SNSC secretary runs the body that coordinates Iran's war, nuclear and negotiation files, and the Leader's representative is the office that ratifies its decisions, so one man now sits on both sides of the approval. That collapses a check the system was built with. The second thing our reader should carry is what the choice signals about the succession: a new Supreme Leader staffing the security apparatus with a founding-generation IRGC commander is buying legitimacy from the institution he most needs not to challenge him, and it tells you which constituency he considers decisive. Establish who Rezaee replaces and why they left, his record — Guards commander 1981–1997, Expediency Council secretary, repeated presidential candidate, and the Argentine AMIA indictment outstanding against him — and what the SNSC has actually decided this year on the US channel and on Hormuz. Attribute carefully across four outlets that agree on the fact and diverge sharply on its meaning: sentiment divergence here is 0.51, with TASS and Mehr reading it as consolidation and Middle East Eye as militarisation. OIC sourcing satisfied: Mehr News (IR) is Tehran's own wire and The National covers it from the Gulf. FEED NOTE for the audit: this 22:00 feed carried only four multi-source clusters. One is the 12 August solar eclipse, already covered three times and with a Hindustan Times astrology column as one of its three sources; the remaining three are selected in this cycle. The economy multi-source floor could not be met — no economy-tagged multi-source cluster in this feed carried economic content, so all three economy picks are single-source. Africa remains unfillable: the only African items in the feed are two Premium Times opinion columns and one promoted item.

stories.label: Curfew imposed in Balochistan Surab's district over law and order concerns
stories.summary: Surab district is under curfew from 8pm to 9am until 15 August, and on the same day the administrations of Upper and Lower South Waziristan and Tank imposed Section 144 across parts of three districts for Monday. Consolidate both into one entry: two provinces, one instrument. Lead with the duration and the hours, because a week-long nightly curfew is not an emergency response — it is a governing schedule. The mechanism our reader should carry is what Section 144 of Pakistan's Criminal Procedure Code actually is: a colonial-era provision, inherited from 1898, that lets a district magistrate ban assembly and movement by executive notification, with no legislative vote, no judicial finding and no expiry beyond the one the order writes for itself — so the legal threshold for suspending movement in a district is a single official's stated apprehension of danger. That is why it renews rather than ends, and why the same districts have lived under it for years at a time. Establish the exact terms and duration of the Surab notification and the Waziristan and Tank orders, what specific incidents the administrations cite, how many days each of these districts has spent under Section 144 or curfew in the past year, whether internet or mobile service was suspended alongside, and what the Balochistan High Court and Peshawar High Court have said about repeat orders. Who is affected: residents of Surab, Wanna and Tank, for whom night hours mean hospital access, and the by-election and political-assembly context in Balochistan that a movement ban forecloses without ever naming it. Name the accountable parties — the deputy commissioners who signed and the provincial governments behind them. OIC sourcing satisfied: Dawn (PK).

stories.label: Moscow rejects option of 'freezing' Ukraine conflict, Russian deputy foreign minister says
stories.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin says Russia will not accept a freeze of the war and that its 'root causes' must be eliminated first. Lead with what 'root causes' has meant in every Russian statement of terms — Ukrainian neutrality, limits on its armed forces, and recognition of the annexations — because the phrase is the position, and reporting it untranslated lets a maximalist demand pass as diplomatic language. The mechanism our reader should carry is why a freeze is the only outcome that has ever ended a war of this shape and why Moscow refuses it anyway: a ceasefire along current lines converts occupied territory into a disputed border and stops the clock on an advance Russia believes is still paying, so rejecting the freeze is a statement about battlefield expectations rather than about principle. Establish exactly what Galuzin said and to whom, how it compares with Putin's stated conditions and with Russia's position at the last talks, what Kyiv and Washington have proposed, and where the front has actually moved in the last quarter. SOURCING DISCIPLINE: TASS is a Russian state agency and is the sole source here; this is legitimate as a primary record of Moscow's own on-the-record position, but attribute every element to Galuzin by name, do not let the ministry's framing stand as description, and seek the Ukrainian and US responses. Follows this file's coverage of the WHO warehouse strike in Dnipro and the North Korean deployment claim — the same week in which Russia says the war cannot be paused.

stories.label: Burnham vows crackdown on 'rip-off' business practices to ease cost of living
stories.summary: The first of the new British prime minister's 'everyday fixes' is a ban on fake discounts and a requirement that subscriptions be as easy to cancel as to start. Lead with what is being regulated rather than with the politics: these are dark patterns, and naming them as a category is what makes the story travel. The mechanism our reader should carry is that both practices monetise the same asymmetry — a retailer who inflates a reference price for six weeks and then 'discounts' it is selling a comparison, not a product, and a subscription with a one-click signup and a phone-only cancellation is charging a fee for the friction it deliberately built. Neither is fraud in any conventional sense, which is precisely why they persisted: the harm is distributed in single-pound increments across millions of people, so no individual has standing worth exercising. Establish what the measures actually require and whether they are primary legislation or CMA guidance, what enforcement powers and penalties attach, when they take effect, the CMA's own estimate of consumer detriment from these practices, and which sectors — gyms, streaming, telecoms, insurance auto-renewal — are in scope. Then the part that generalises past Britain: the EU's Digital Fairness Act, India's dark-pattern guidelines and the FTC's click-to-cancel rule are converging on the same conduct from three different legal traditions, and the UK is now legislating what the US courts struck down. Who holds power: the firms whose renewal revenue depends on the friction, and a regulator whose penalty ceiling determines whether compliance is cheaper than the practice.

stories.label: Hyperliquid's RWA perps boom is eating into the revenue that backs HYPE
stories.summary: Hyperliquid has never traded more contracts and has never kept a smaller share of what those contracts earn — open interest hit $11 billion on 13 July while the platform's own take rate fell. Lead with those two curves crossing, because the divergence is the finding and it is the exact opposite of what volume growth is normally read to mean. The mechanism our reader should carry is where the revenue goes: perpetual futures on real-world assets — equities, treasuries, commodities — require the venue to pay a market maker to hold the other side and to source a price feed it does not own, so each RWA contract carries a cost structure that a crypto-native perp does not, and growth in the product mix dilutes the fee margin even as notional volume rises. That matters beyond one exchange because HYPE, the token, is valued on the platform's fee buybacks: the asset is a claim on revenue, so a falling take rate repricing it is a straightforward equity-style earnings problem wearing a token's clothes. This is the same discriminant our crypto shakeout piece identified — whether revenue arrives in money someone else issued — applied to a survivor rather than to the failures, and it shows the test has a second edge. Establish the take-rate figures and their trend, the RWA share of open interest, how much HYPE has been bought back and at what pace, who the designated market makers are and what they are paid, and which oracle supplies the RWA prices. State the regulatory exposure plainly: offering leveraged exposure to US equities offshore is a perimeter question that has not been tested.

stories.label: IRIS2 Gets Green Light With More Money and More Satellites
stories.summary: The European Commission, ESA and the SpaceRISE consortium have cleared IRIS2 for full implementation after seven months of renegotiation, and the programme emerges with both a larger constellation and a larger bill. Lead with the two revised numbers together — satellite count and cost — because a review that raises both is telling you the original figure was a bid, not an estimate. The mechanism our reader should carry is why sovereign satellite constellations cost what they do: capacity scales with the number of spacecraft in view, so any constellation that promises continuous secure coverage is committed to a satellite count set by orbital geometry rather than by budget, and a programme that under-counted at proposal must either buy the difference later or deliver less service. That is the structural reason public space procurement reprices upward and commercial competitors do not appear to. Then the part that matters outside Europe: IRIS2 exists because European governments concluded that renting secure communications from a single American commercial provider is a dependency, not a saving — the same conclusion Iran reached about launchers, India about navigation, and that Gulf and Southeast Asian states are now reaching about ground infrastructure. Establish the revised cost and satellite count against the original 2023 figures, the public–private split and which firms are in SpaceRISE, the service-entry date and how far it has slipped, what the review actually validated, and what Europe currently pays commercial providers for the capacity IRIS2 is meant to replace. Who holds power: a consortium of incumbent European operators negotiating with the only customer that can fund the thing.

stories.label: Flight cancellations, evacuations as China braces for Typhoon Dolphin
stories.summary: Dolphin crossed Okinawa and made landfall on China's east coast as the most powerful cyclone to reach the country this year, with mass evacuations, schools and tourist sites shut and flights grounded across Zhejiang and Fujian. Lead with the evacuation number rather than the wind speed, because the people moved is the measure of the threat as the state itself assessed it. The mechanism our reader should carry is why this coast in particular: the East China Sea has been running well above its seasonal average temperature, and a cyclone's intensity is set by the heat available in the upper ocean layer it crosses, so warm water along the final approach is what prevents the weakening that landfalling storms historically showed — the storm arrives at close to peak rather than spent. That is the specific, physical way a warming ocean changes a typhoon, and it is more useful to a reader than the word 'unprecedented'. Establish the landfall intensity and central pressure, how many people were evacuated and from which provinces, rainfall totals and the flooding risk in the Yangtze delta, what damage Okinawa recorded first, and how Dolphin compares with the strongest storms to hit Zhejiang in the past decade. Then the exposure that travels: the same coast holds Ningbo-Zhoushan and Shanghai, the world's two busiest container ports, so a storm that closes them for days reaches every importer downstream. Attribute forecasts to the China Meteorological Administration and the Japan Meteorological Agency separately — their intensity scales differ and the numbers will not match.

stories.label: Wales 'left behind' after Jesy Nelson SMA screening 'victory'
stories.summary: England will start screening newborns for spinal muscular atrophy and Wales will not, so from a date now fixed two babies born on either side of a border will get different medical futures. Lead with that border, not with the celebrity campaign that won the change — the campaign is how the decision was made, and that is itself the accountability problem. The mechanism our reader should carry is why SMA screening is unusually time-critical: the disease destroys motor neurons from birth, the gene therapies and antisense drugs that treat it can only preserve neurons that are still alive, and infants are typically diagnosed after symptoms appear, by which point the loss is permanent. So the screening test is not early detection of a treatable disease — it is the difference between treatment working and not working, measured in weeks. That is what makes a devolved decision on a heel-prick panel a decision about which children walk. Establish when England's screening begins, what the UK National Screening Committee recommended and to whom that recommendation applies, what the Welsh Government has actually said and what it says the obstacle is, the cost per screen against the cost of the therapies — nusinersen and onasemnogene are among the most expensive drugs ever licensed, which is the fiscal argument screening should win — and the position in Scotland and Northern Ireland. Who is affected and who is accountable: parents in Wales, and a devolved health department that can be asked for a date. The pattern generalises to any federal health system where a screening panel is set below the national level.

stories.label: Fastmail offers EU data region
stories.summary: An Australian email provider will now store customer mail in the EU rather than the United States, and 493 points on Hacker News says developers understood immediately why that is not a feature announcement. Lead with the jurisdiction, not the datacentre: where a mailbox physically sits determines which government can compel its disclosure without telling the account holder. The mechanism our reader should carry is the US CLOUD Act — it reaches data held by US-connected providers wherever in the world the servers are, which means an EU data region only closes the exposure if the operating company, and not merely the disk, is outside American jurisdiction. So the question to put to any provider offering this is corporate structure, not geography, and most of the answers are worse than the marketing. Establish what Fastmail actually moved and what remains in the US, its corporate domicile and whether that places it inside or outside CLOUD Act reach, what Australia's own Assistance and Access Act obliges it to do, whether the service is end-to-end encrypted at rest (if the provider holds the keys, the jurisdiction question is the only question), and what it costs. Then the part that matters most to our readers: this choice does not exist for most of the world. A user in Pakistan, Egypt or Nigeria picking between Gmail and a European host is choosing which foreign government can read their mail, because the domestic option is either absent or worse — and every state that has tried to build one has built a surveillance requirement into it. Data residency is sovereignty for those who can buy it.

stories.label: Controlled cracking technique prints quantum dots into tiny pixels for sharper displays
stories.summary: Researchers are patterning quantum dots into display pixels by deliberately cracking a film — letting a material fail along controlled lines instead of etching it. Lead with that inversion, because it is genuinely counterintuitive and it is the technique: fracture is what fabrication normally spends its budget preventing, and here the crack is the tool. The mechanism our reader should carry is why quantum dots resist conventional patterning at all — they are colloidal nanocrystals held in a ligand shell, and the photolithography that patterns silicon uses solvents and developers that strip that shell and kill the luminescence, so the industry has been stuck depositing them as a uniform colour-conversion layer over a blue backlight rather than as independently addressable red and green emitters. Direct patterning is the step between quantum dots as a filter and quantum dots as the light source, which is the difference in efficiency and colour that the QD-EL displays now being promised depend on. Give the actual numbers: the pixel pitch and pixels-per-inch achieved, how it compares with inkjet-printed and photolithographic QD patterning, the luminance and colour-gamut figures, and whether the process survives at panel scale or only on laboratory coupons. State the limits plainly — controlled cracking is a stochastic process being asked to hit deterministic positions, and yield across a large substrate is the whole commercial question. Who holds power: display patterning IP concentrates in a handful of Korean, Chinese and Japanese manufacturers, and where the technique is licensed determines who builds the next generation of panels.

stories.label: An interpretable metaheuristic-optimized RVFL architecture for robust CO₂ emissions prediction in decarbonizing energy systems
stories.summary: A machine-learning model for forecasting national CO₂ emissions is being offered with 'interpretable' in its title, and the word is doing more work than the architecture. Lead with what interpretability is actually claimed to be here, because that is the reviewable part: a random vector functional link network is a neural network with randomly fixed hidden weights and only the output layer trained, which makes it fast and cheap but does not make it explicable — so any interpretability comes from a feature-attribution method bolted on afterwards, and attribution is a description of the model's behaviour, not of the world. The mechanism our reader should carry is why that distinction has consequences: emissions forecasts are inputs to NDC targets, carbon budgets and infrastructure finance, and a model that reports which of its inputs moved its output is routinely read as reporting which policies reduce emissions. It is not. Establish which countries and years the model was trained on, what its inputs are (GDP, energy mix, population are the usual set, and their collinearity is the hard problem), the error figures against the standard baselines — including whether it beats a simple extrapolation, which these papers often do not report — which metaheuristic was used to tune it and how much of the gain came from tuning rather than architecture, and whether the code and data are available. State the limits plainly: this is an unedited early-access manuscript, and the honest framing is a forecasting tool for countries without the modelling capacity of an OECD environment ministry — which is a real gap worth filling — rather than a policy instrument. Global South energy ministries are exactly who ends up using models like this.

stories.label: Syria makes deal to take back control of Russian bases
stories.summary: Damascus says it has agreed with Moscow on the future of Hmeimim airbase and the Tartus naval facility — the two installations that kept Assad in power and that give Russia its only warm-water Mediterranean port. Lead with what 'taking back control' actually means in the text: whether Russia keeps use of the sites under a Syrian-signed lease, on what term, and who pays. The mechanism for the reader is that basing rights survive the government that granted them — a new Syrian state inherits the facilities but also inherits Moscow's leverage over reconstruction, wheat and the UN Security Council seat that shields it. Attribute carefully: SANA and the Syrian foreign ministry are the only primary sources for the terms, TASS is reporting Moscow's read, and neither has published a document. Note what Russia gains from a legalised presence it previously held by force.

stories.label: Pakistani hostages held by Somali pirates issue new distress message seeking govt help
stories.summary: The crew of the Palau-flagged tanker MT Honour 25 have been held more than 100 days and are now appealing directly to Islamabad by video because no one else has an obligation to them. Lead with the number of days and the flag: a Palau flag of convenience means the vessel's nominal state has no navy, the owner's insurers negotiate privately, and the crew's own government has no legal duty to a ship it did not register. That is the mechanism — flag-of-convenience registration transfers a seafarer's protection from a state to a commercial contract, and when the contract stalls the crew waits. Establish how many of the 17-18 crew are Pakistani, who the registered owner and manager are, what the Foreign Office and the Pakistan Navy have said, whether EU NAVFOR Atalanta or the Indian Navy are engaged, and how many hijackings off Somalia have been recorded since the 2024 resurgence. OIC sourcing satisfied: Dawn (PK); no Somali outlet in this feed.

stories.label: Russia destroys World Health Organization warehouse in Dnipro
stories.summary: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus confirmed a WHO warehouse in Dnipro was destroyed in a Russian strike, burning emergency medical stock. Lead with what was inside and how many facilities it supplied, not with the building. The mechanism: humanitarian logistics concentrate — one warehouse serves dozens of hospitals across an oblast, so a single strike removes months of resupply from a whole region, and replacement runs through the same corridors that are being struck. Establish WHO's own accounting of attacks on health care in Ukraine (its Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care has a running count), whether the warehouse was deconflicted with Moscow under the UN notification mechanism, and what Russia's defence ministry says it was aiming at. Name the accountable party plainly and note that deconflicted humanitarian sites carry protected status under international humanitarian law.

stories.label: Ukraine's Zelensky Claims Russia To Deploy 50,000 North Korean Troops
stories.summary: Zelensky put the figure at up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers and did not say where it came from — treat the unsourced number as the story's first fact, not its headline. What is verifiable is the exchange behind it: Pyongyang has been supplying manpower and shells, and Zelensky's warning is that it is being paid in anti-air and missile know-how it could not otherwise buy. Lead with that trade, because it is the part with consequences past this war — a sanctioned state converting expendable labour into air-defence technology reprices the security of Seoul and Tokyo. Establish what South Korea's NIS and Western intelligence have publicly assessed the current deployment to be, how those numbers compare with the 50,000 claim, what DPRK casualties have been reported, and what Pyongyang and Moscow acknowledge under their 2024 mutual defence treaty. Mark every figure with who asserted it.

stories.label: AIPAC-Linked Super PACs, Pro-Israel Donors Flood Primary to Succeed Angie Craig With More Than $3 Million
stories.summary: More than $3 million from AIPAC-linked super PACs and Democratic Majority for Israel has landed in a single open-seat Democratic primary in Minnesota's 2nd district, aimed at the progressive in a three-way race. Lead with the ratio, not the total: outside money measured against what the candidates themselves raised is what shows the mechanism, which is that a super PAC can outspend an entire campaign in the final fortnight and never appear on the candidate's own filings. Establish the named vehicles (UDP, DMFI PAC), their FEC-reported totals and the dates of the buys, what each candidate raised directly, and whether the ads mention Israel at all — the pattern in comparable races has been ads on crime and prescription drugs funded by a foreign-policy PAC, which is precisely the accountability gap. Drop Site is a single source; anchor every figure to the FEC filing rather than to the outlet's characterisation.

stories.label: Alexandria's Amreya shuts factory to striking workers
stories.summary: Management at Misr al-Amreya Spinning and Weaving suspended operations indefinitely and called it routine maintenance; four workers told Mada Masr it is retaliation for their strike over underpayment. Lead with the gap between the two accounts, because the shutdown is the mechanism — an indefinite closure converts a strike into a lockout, stops the wages the strike was about, and does it without a single dismissal that a labour court could review. Establish the headcount affected, what the pay dispute is actually about (which allowance or bonus, and how far it lags inflation), whether an independent union or the state-run ETUF is representing them, what the Manpower Ministry has done, and Amreya's ownership — this is one of Egypt's large public-sector textile mills, so the employer and the regulator sit close together. Egypt's textile strikes are the country's most persistent labour action and almost never reach Western wires. OIC sourcing satisfied: Mada Masr (EG).

stories.label: Crypto is going through a massive dot-com style shakeout as over 100 projects fold in 2026
stories.summary: More than 100 crypto projects have shut down, gone bankrupt or gone dark in 2026, and the survivors share one trait: they charge fees in stablecoins or cash rather than paying users in their own token. Lead with the count and the discriminant together. The mechanism worth teaching is token-emission financing — a project that pays for growth by printing its own token is funding operations out of future dilution, which works only while the price rises, so the shakeout is a repricing of that model rather than of the technology. Establish who counted the 100 and how (which tracker, what 'gone dark' means), how much capital the failures locked up, what fees the survivors named actually collect, and how this compares with the 2018 and 2022 washouts. The reader's takeaway is a test they can apply to any platform: does revenue arrive in money someone else issued?

stories.label: Turkish shipowner to sue Ukraine with ICC for attacks on its vessel
stories.summary: The owner of the Turkish bulk carrier MV Reyhan Sari, hit by a drone in the Black Sea on 22 July while carrying Russian coal from Taman to Trabzon, says it will take the case to an international court. Lead with the forum problem: the International Criminal Court prosecutes individuals for international crimes and does not award damages to companies, so a shipowner's real remedies are war-risk insurance, a claim under the Turkish-flag state's protection, or arbitration — and which forum is actually named will tell the reader whether this is litigation or signalling. The mechanism that matters to Turkey is pricing: every drone strike on a merchant hull raises Black Sea war-risk premiums for neutral carriers, and Turkish owners carry a large share of that trade. Establish the vessel's flag, owner and insurer, what Kyiv says about the strike, how many neutral-flag merchant ships have been hit since the corridor reopened, and what war-risk rates have done. TASS is a Russian state agency and the only source here — attribute the intent-to-sue to the owner and seek Turkish confirmation; no Turkish outlet appears in this feed.

stories.label: Mount Toba eruption doesn't seem like it could nearly kill our species
stories.summary: The Toba supereruption on Sumatra 74,000 years ago emptied thousands of cubic kilometres of magma in about two weeks — a thousand Pinatubos — and for decades it anchored the claim that humanity was reduced to a few thousand survivors. New work says the climate forcing was not enough. Lead with what the evidence actually is: sulfur dioxide yield estimated from the deposits, and what that implies for years of cooling, versus what the genetic bottleneck signal really shows. The mechanism to teach is that a bottleneck in the genome is a date range, not a cause, and attaching it to the nearest catastrophe is the error being corrected. Establish who did the work and how the new SO2 estimate was derived, what the revised cooling figure is, and what this means for the volcanic-winter models that inform present-day risk planning — Indonesia still hosts the caldera and 270 million people.

stories.label: Timeline of the OpenAI accidental attack against Hugging Face
stories.summary: A misconfigured OpenAI system generated enough traffic to take down parts of Hugging Face — the repository nearly every open-weights model in the world is downloaded from, including the ones Global South labs depend on because they cannot rent frontier compute. Lead with the asymmetry: one company's retry loop is a denial-of-service against shared public infrastructure, and no contract, SLA or regulator sits between them. The mechanism to explain is why it happens — aggressive client-side retries with no backoff multiply a failing request into a flood, which is the same pattern behind the AI-crawler load now hitting Wikipedia, SourceHut and small archives. Establish the timeline from Willison's write-up, what Hugging Face and OpenAI each said, how long degradation lasted, and what mitigation was applied. Ask the accountability question directly: who pays for the bandwidth when a trillion-dollar model provider overruns a free host?

stories.label: Iran to launch 3 new satellites before year end
stories.summary: Iran's ICT minister Sattar Hashemi says three satellites of the 'Martyr Soleimani' constellation will go up on a single mission before the Iranian year ends in March. Lead with the launcher question, not the payload: whether these fly on an Iranian vehicle or on a Russian Soyuz from Vostochny — as Khayyam and the Pars satellites did — is the difference between an indigenous space capability and a purchased orbital slot, and it is the fact the announcement is least likely to volunteer. The mechanism for our reader is that a satellite constellation under sanctions is built from what you can launch, not what you can build; every commercial launch contract signed with Moscow is also a dependency. Establish the stated masses and orbits, the intended function (imaging, comms or navigation), the launch provider, and Iran's actual orbital record versus its announced schedule — the gap between the two has been wide. Mehr is Iranian state media: attribute the plan as a ministerial claim, not an accomplished launch.

stories.label: “Code was never the hard part” is an insult to all programmers
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for tech floor] 823 points, 497 comments on Hacker News
